concepts.name: Signed self-adjoint window operator K_A = L_A - M_A + P_A
concepts.plain: The window Weil form is the form of one closed, semibounded self-adjoint operator: a positive jump (Gamma plus primes) operator, minus a constant mass, plus a rank-two pole part. The Gamma part grows like log|t| in frequency. The operator exists; its sign on E0 is exactly what is missing.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: On L2(I_A), I_A = [-A/2, A/2], the form W = P + H_A - M_A||F||^2 is closed and bounded below on a log-Sobolev domain; the associated operator is K_A = L_A - M_A + P_A with L_A >= 0 the Gamma and prime jump operator and P_A of rank 2. The Gamma symbol is asymptotic to log|t|. The missing inequality is ||J_A F||^2 >= M_A ||F||^2 on E0 (J_A the square root of L_A) proved without zeros.
concepts.formula: K_A = L_A - M_A + P_A,  W(F) = <K_A F, F>
concepts.uncertain: Positivity of K_A on E0 for any window beyond A = 1.1.
concepts.proved: Closedness and semiboundedness from the positive jump form plus bounded perturbations (operator2023).
concepts.tests: Any proposed sign mechanism must reproduce the certified gaps on A <= 1.1.
pitfalls: Existence of a self-adjoint operator is not a sign statement.
Do not identify K_A with the cusp Laplacian: same 1/4, different operator.

rels.note: B is the L_A - M_A part

concepts.name: Pole-cancelled ledger with Chebyshev remainder
concepts.plain: Subtracting the pole against the main term of the prime sum rewrites W with a constant K5 = K0 + 4 and an integral against the Chebyshev remainder E = psi - x. The unconstrained residual mass changes sign between A = 1 and A = 2.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: W(F) = K5||F||^2 + J5(F) - 2 int x^{-1/2} <F, T_{log x}F> dE(x), E = psi_Cheb - x, K5(0) = K0 + 4. Unconstrained residual mass M~_A = M_A - 4e^{A/2}.
concepts.uncertain: Sign control of the dE integral on E0.
concepts.tests: Ghost n=2 deletion changes the dE term.
pitfalls: sos2010 "Lemma A" is a Ritz value, not a lower bound.

concepts.name: E0 = (d^2 - 1/4) H^2_0: moment constraints as a Hardy-1/4 operator
concepts.plain: Every window test with both moments zero is (d^2 - 1/4)G for a unique G supported in the window, and conversely. In the chart r = e^{-u} the operator is d_r(r^2 d_r); 1/4 is the Hardy constant and also the bottom of the continuous spectrum at the modular cusp.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: D = d^2 - 1/4 maps H^2_0(I_A) bijectively onto L2(I_A) ∩ ker C+ ∩ ker C-, C± = ∫F e^{±u/2}. Under r = e^{-u} with the unitary half-density, D becomes d_r(r^2 d_r). The radial cusp operator -y^2 d_y^2 is unitarily -d_t^2 + 1/4.
concepts.uncertain: Whether the shared 1/4 is more than coincidence of half-densities.
concepts.proved: Elementary ODE with compact support iff both moments vanish (parabola2019, poincare2024, modular2026).
pitfalls: Same constant 1/4 does not make the cusp Laplacian the W operator.

concepts.name: M_A as a regularized prime sum fixed by the character class
concepts.plain: The mass M_A is twice the window prime sum minus its regularized value -zeta'/zeta(1/2) = K0/2. The constant K0 has the closed form -(gamma + log 8 pi + pi/2) and is fixed by the adelic character class; there is no free renormalization parameter. The SL2(Z) cusp produces the sigma = 1 version of the constant instead.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: M_A = 2(S_A - S_reg), S_reg = -zeta'/zeta(1/2) = K0/2; -K0 = gamma + log 8pi + pi/2; FP∫k = pi/2 + 2log2; in Connes semilocal trace degree form M_A is the total alpha-normalized mass. K0 - K0^(1) = -pi/2 - log 2.
concepts.proved: Closed forms checked to 30 digits (audit2060); Connes 1999 Thm VII.4 cited for the trace form.
pitfalls: The earlier "RG family" reading (free scheme parameter) is wrong.
Explicit-formula tables of M_A that use zeros are diagnostics only.

concepts.name: No-prime windows: W >= 0.1965||F||^2 on E0 for A <= 1/10
concepts.plain: For windows shorter than log 2 no prime enters, and a Poincare-type argument using both moment constraints proves a uniform positive lower bound for A <= 1/10.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: For A <= 1/10, W(F) >= c*||F||^2 on E0 with c* = log(5√2/π) - γ - 3/80 ≈ 0.19657 > 7/240. Elementary chain bounds without moments fail at A = 1 (3.7528 vs 6.3524 needed).
concepts.proved: Hand proof (poincare2024), constant rechecked in audit2060.
pitfalls: No prime is involved; this says nothing about arithmetic.

concepts.name: Certified E0 gaps through A = 1.1 (primes 2 and 3)
concepts.plain: Three computer-assisted bounds: W >= 0.0045||F||^2 on E0 up to width 0.694 (interval arithmetic), W >= 0.004||F||^2 up to width 1 (prime 2), and W >= 0.0005||F||^2 up to width 1.1 (primes 2 and 3). Beyond 1.1 nothing is certified.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: A <= 347/500: constrained log-Jensen lemma, mpmath.iv. A <= 1: 815 cells, N=48, κ=2; finite eigenvalue > 0.0069963, h* > 2.2304, B* < 0.07587, Schur margin > 0.000314 ⇒ W >= ||F||^2/250. A <= 1.1: 1838 cells, N=192, κ=4; effective eigenvalue > 0.00066384, h* > 3.20786 ⇒ W >= 0.0005||F||^2. Computer-assisted: scalar data in mpmath interval arithmetic; finite matrices in IEEE-754 binary64 with dot-product error gamma_n = n u/(1 - n u), u = 2^-53, and explicit residual/orthogonality bounds. Not a formally verified proof.
concepts.uncertain: Extension past 1.1; formal verification of the floating-point layer.
concepts.proved: Computer-assisted: scalar data in mpmath interval arithmetic; finite matrices in IEEE-754 binary64 with dot-product error gamma_n = n u/(1 - n u), u = 2^-53, and explicit residual/orthogonality bounds. Not a formally verified proof. Re-executed with single-thread BLAS; all assertions passed.
concepts.tests: Same pipeline with n=2 deleted must fail (ghost control).
pitfalls: Not a formal proof.
Window positivity on A <= 1.1 is not RH and is not all-window positivity.
Failure of the interval bound at 0.695 is inconclusive, not a counterexample.

concepts.name: E0 minima beyond A = 1.1 are numerical and grid-biased
concepts.plain: Constrained minima of W/||F||^2 fall from about 0.012 at A = 1 to about 1.3e-5 for A between 2 and 3 on 2048-cell models; 128-cell models give about 2e-3, roughly 100 times larger. The gap and the discretization error are the same size.
concepts.label: Numerical
numbers: 2048 cells vs 128 cells differ ~100x beyond A ≈ 1.1
pitfalls: Upper estimates only; do not draw as brackets.
A tiny positive minimum is not evidence of positivity at that scale.

concepts.name: Deleting n = 2 alone makes W negative on an explicit E0 test
concepts.plain: On the test (d^2 - 1/4)(1-u^2)^4 at width 2, the true W/||F||^2 is +0.0023; deleting only the n = 2 term gives -0.639. Any positivity proof must see the actual prime coefficients.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: G = (1-u^2)^4 on [-1,1], F = DG, ||F||^2 = 40.77466; W = 0.0951580, W/N = 0.0023338; drop-2 W/N = -0.63923 (two routes: physical quadrature and Fourier side).
concepts.proved: Quadrature in two independent routes agree.
pitfalls: The deleted-coefficient form is not admissible Euler data; it is a sensitivity control, not a counterexample.

concepts.name: Exactly one negative direction off E0 (certified at A = 1, 1.1)
concepts.plain: With Q = W - P on the full window, n-(Q|E0) = n-(Q) + n+(S) - 2 where S is the 2x2 moment Schur complement. At A = 1 and 1.1 the certificate shows Q has exactly one negative direction and the rest of its spectrum is at least 0.004 and 0.0005. The sign pattern of S follows from the constrained certificate, not independently.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: A=1: Q(const) ∈ [-1.95450, -1.95400], second spectral lower 0.004, Schur margin 0.000513. A=1.1: Q(const) ∈ [-2.1351, -2.1346], gap 0.0005, margin 0.000164. Finite minorant W_J alone has 2 negative directions. Scans to A=3: n-(Q)=1 in every finite model; squared overlap of the negative mode with span{e^{±u/2}} 0.969–0.999. Computer-assisted: scalar data in mpmath interval arithmetic; finite matrices in IEEE-754 binary64 with dot-product error gamma_n = n u/(1 - n u), u = 2^-53, and explicit residual/orthogonality bounds. Not a formally verified proof.
concepts.proved: Computer-assisted: scalar data in mpmath interval arithmetic; finite matrices in IEEE-754 binary64 with dot-product error gamma_n = n u/(1 - n u), u = 2^-53, and explicit residual/orthogonality bounds. Not a formally verified proof.
concepts.tests: A class map Φ must reproduce this count and gap.
pitfalls: One negative direction, not two.
Overlap 0.97–0.999 is closeness, not identity with the hyperbolic plane.
S signature is derived from, not independent of, the E0 certificate.

rels.note: negative mode near the pole plane

concepts.name: Boundary plane (1,1) and the FE-fixed class e = h + v
concepts.plain: The two boundary classes h, v are isotropic with J(h,v) = 1, so they span a hyperbolic plane of signature (1,1). The functional equation swaps them; the fixed class e = h + v has J(e,e) = 2, normalized by the residues -1, +1 of the completed zeta at s = 0, 1. Its orthogonal complement contains the negative line h - v as well as the projected tests, so it is not E0.
concepts.label: Theorem
pitfalls: Residues are those of the completed zeta Λ(s), not of ξ (ξ is entire).

concepts.name: Formal boundary model: -J(πF, πG) = W is a restatement
concepts.plain: Adding the two boundary classes and projecting, πF = F - C-(F)h - C+(F)v, gives -J(πF, πG) = W(F, G) on every window test. Because J on tests is defined from W, this reproduces the Hodge-index layout but proves nothing about the sign.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: With J defined on tests by J|tests = -W - (pole correction), the projection identity holds on all of D(I). A sign theorem needs J constructed independently, with W = -(intersection) on the primitive sector computed.
pitfalls: Do not cite this identity as evidence for a Hodge index theorem.

concepts.name: Requirements on the missing arithmetic class map Φ
concepts.plain: A real Hodge-index route needs a map Φ from window tests to an intersection space built from geometry first, for example Φ(F) = ∫F(u)[Γ_u]du over graphs of the scaling action. The pairing must be computed: primes as fixed points with weight Λ(n)/√n, the Gamma term as an archimedean Green term, M_A as the diagonal self-intersection, and a Hodge-index theorem that applies. A fixed finite-rank lattice cannot work.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Tests for any candidate: reproduce exactly one negative direction off E0 with gaps ≥ 0.004 (A=1) and ≥ 0.0005 (A=1.1); see the n=2 coefficient (ghost control). Ingredient status: ampleness holds on the positive-function cone; effectivity fails for the pointwise cone; a relative (GRR-type) lemma gives (A)+(R) ⇒ n+(J)=1; quadratic Riemann–Roch missing.
concepts.formula: Φ(F) = ∫ F(u) [Γ_u] du,  W = -⟨ΦF, ΦF⟩ on the primitive sector
concepts.tests: Finite certificates (A ≤ 1.1) and the n=2 ghost.
pitfalls: A pairing defined from W is circular.
Finite-rank NS obstruction (bulk_form_B_off_E0).

rels.note: concrete shape of the missing object

concepts.name: W = half the minimal pencil discriminant through e
concepts.plain: Every window test spans with the boundary classes a pencil of conics; W(F) is half the minimum of its discriminant through e. Window lines become nearly parabolic as A grows, and a four-dimensional example shows the conic picture alone does not force positivity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: W(F) = ½ min Δ_e; disc(Q|ℓ) = -4 det M · Q(pole ℓ); one conic in a moving chart, det = -1/4. Separation 0.128, 1.46e-3, 1.6e-7 [Numerical].
pitfalls: Geometry of the pencil does not supply a sign.

concepts.name: K0 is a Mellin derivative, not an Arakelov degree on P^1_Z
concepts.plain: The arithmetic self-intersection of the diagonal on P^1 over Z is 2 - 4a for the canonical metric family, never -K0. K0 is the derivative 2(log Γ_R)'(1/2) (= 2E[log|x|] under the Tate weight). The Tate dimension-one diagonal has degree 0. Hecke ratios at weight 12 are 2cos(mθ_p), which do not collapse to Λ(n)/√n.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ω̂^2(P^1_Z) = 2 - 4a; -K0 - (2-4a) = 3.3722, 5.3722, 1.0827, -0.3036 for the canonical choices tested. Derived Δ^2 = 2 - 2g.
pitfalls: Scope: P^1_Z and the metrics tested.
Spin/Wu/Rokhlin structures give parity only.

rels.note: P^1_Z diagonal does not produce K0

concepts.name: B_W(F_z, F_w) = K_q(z, w): W on exponential probes is the ξ response kernel
concepts.plain: On truncated exponentials F_z = e^{-zu}1_{u≥0}, the complete Weil form, including pole, Gamma, K0 and every prime, equals the kernel (q(z) + conj q(w))/(z + conj w) with q = ξ'/ξ(1/2 + z). RH is equivalent to q being positive-real (Lagarias, Hinkkanen); the passage from probes back to compact tests is only sketched.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: For Re z, Re w > 1/2: B_W(F_z, F_w) = K_q(z, w). Inverse superposition to compact tests: sketched.
concepts.uncertain: Full proof of "PSD on one vertical line ⇒ W ≥ 0 on compact tests".
concepts.proved: Exact algebra (dispersion2030); three probe pairs rechecked by independent quadrature in audit2060.
pitfalls: q'(0) > 0 is not passivity (z + z^3 is a falsifier).

concepts.name: Causal and dispersive is not passive
concepts.plain: Explicit causal, stable transfer functions such as -1/(z+1), the ghost transfer, and z + z^3 fail positive-realness. Anomalous dispersion is not loss, and Heaviside's distortionless line is still lossy. The needed property is Herglotz positivity, not causality.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Falsifiers: q = -1/(z+1); q_a (ghost); z + z^3.
pitfalls: Distortionless ≠ lossless.

concepts.name: Delay-line realization with signed KYP storage
concepts.plain: The ξ response has a delay-line state realization whose storage identity is exact but signed: the boundary storage 2Re(x+ conj x-) is indefinite. A finite prime cutoff leaves a pole at z = 1/2, and independent per-prime storage diverges.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: 2Re(ū y_B) = d/dt(S_∂ + S_jump) + D_jump - M_B|u|^2; pole-cancelled transfer q = g5 - ∫x^{-z-1/2} dE.
pitfalls: A signed storage identity is not a passivity proof.

concepts.name: Prime-gap 2x2 storage blocks fail
concepts.plain: Coupling the storage blocks with a fixed PSD diagonal diverges, and the exact-match block is not PSD inside prime gaps: at cutoff B = 2 the weight w_B is negative just after log 2, 3, 5 and 7, proved at s = 49/25.
concepts.label: Theorem
pitfalls: Scope: these block shapes only.

concepts.name: Bost–Connes KMS at β = 1/2 gives the prime weights but not K_q
concepts.plain: At β = 1/2 the Bost–Connes KMS state produces vectors with squared norm Λ(n)/√n exactly, but their Gram kernel is -ζ'/ζ(1/2 + z + conj w), which lacks the Gamma, pole and mass terms of K_q; the all-prime vector has infinite norm. The fermion primon gas has the wrong sign at n = 4 and 9.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ||v_n||^2 = Λ(n)/√n; kernel -ζ'/ζ(1/2 + z + w̄) ≠ K_q; boson Z = ζ(β), fermion Z = ζ(β)/ζ(2β).
pitfalls: Positive weights are not positive W.

concepts.name: Gamma jump kernel as a Planck/OU ladder
concepts.plain: The archimedean jump kernel e^{-a/2}/(1 - e^{-2a}) is the sum of exponentials with rates 2m + 1/2, a Planck-type ladder. Reading Gamma as radiation and primes as a primon gas is suggestive; they are not one Hamiltonian, and kinetic (H_A) versus potential (M_A) is bookkeeping, not a sign mechanism.
concepts.label: Analogy
pitfalls: Not a thermodynamic proof of positivity.

concepts.name: Serre derivative of E_k closes only at k = 4, 6, 8, 12
concepts.plain: Differentiating E_k and restoring covariance with E_2 leaves a cusp correction f_k in S_{k+2}; it vanishes exactly when S_{k+2} = 0. For E_10 the correction carries 38016/691. This is a calibration of the derivative anomaly, not a W mechanism.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.proved: Bernoulli bound plus exact check 14 ≤ k ≤ 398 (eisenstein1990); 38016/691 rechecked in audit2060.
pitfalls: E_2 = θ log Δ vs K0 = 2(log Γ_R)'(1/2) is a parallel, not an identification.

concepts.name: X^10 - 1 is the boundary class δ(1) in H^1_c; Eisenstein denominator 691
concepts.plain: In weight 12 the period polynomial X^10 - 1 is the boundary class δ(1) in compactly supported cohomology, not the Eisenstein class. The Eisenstein lift has denominator 691 (3617 at weight 16), and mod 691 the Hecke operator T2 + 24 is nilpotent on the Δ line. One cusp supplies only one moment; two moments need Γ0(N).
concepts.label: Theorem
pitfalls: hodge1991 called X^10 - 1 "the Eisenstein class": corrected.
